## Work type
Feature / integration program tracker.

## Current integration scope — owner update, 2026-10-19

**Implement and integrate now:** GitHub (BE-07), MLflow (BE-12), OR-Tools (BE-11), and ERPNext/Frappe (BE-13), with the shared invocation/private-binding/worker/MCP prerequisites that each needs (BE-05/06/08/09). Preserve the ongoing catalog and both native/standalone UI assignments.

**RDKit is optional and deferred to #32.** BE-10 is not a blocker for this delivery. OR-Tools is the first compute-wrapper acceptance example instead. The broad industry/persona catalog remains a roadmap rather than a claim that every integration is operational.

**Testing environment:** the owner selected disposable local test services first. Use real local MLflow/ERPNext services where feasible and bounded protocol fixtures for failure cases. Record a fixture/stub as such; it is not a full ERPNext or MLflow deployment. Do not connect production accounts or claim hosted ChatGPT acceptance from local results.

### Active implementation sequence
1. Complete/reuse the catalog contract and the generic typed invocation/private-binding foundations.
2. GitHub: native connector/official MCP capability mapping with provenance, plus executable read-only operations and read-only local conformance fixtures.
3. MLflow: experiment/run/metric/artifact-metadata retrieval against a disposable tracking service.
4. OR-Tools: actual pinned solver-backed scheduling worker, with valid/invalid/infeasible/time-limited cases and structured statuses.
5. ERPNext/Frappe: company-scoped inventory/work-order reads against a disposable test service; preserve tenant isolation and pagination.
6. Expose operations and requirements through the shared catalog, native tool route and standalone configuration UI, with separate implementation/test/host/release evidence.

Backend owns runtime implementation; Frontend consumes the shared status/configuration contract; QA independently checks deterministic results, failure paths, auth/tenant boundaries and host evidence. Use separate reviewable PRs/slices rather than making all connectors one mandatory package dependency.

- [ ] GitHub: implemented, integrated, locally checked, independently accepted.
- [ ] MLflow: implemented, integrated, disposable-service checked, independently accepted.
- [ ] OR-Tools: implemented with real solver, integrated, independently accepted.
- [ ] ERPNext/Frappe: implemented, integrated, disposable-service checked, independently accepted.
- [ ] Native and standalone exposure agree on requirements and actual support status.
- [ ] Unavailable live/native-host combinations remain explicitly unverified.


## Outcome
Let a user bootstrap a company from composable role templates, selected skill packs and bounded workflows, then connect the necessary tools through supported native GitHub, Codex and ChatGPT surfaces. A new industry should normally require reviewed declarative content and an existing adapter, rather than another hard-coded product branch.

This issue tracks a proposed catalog and implementation backlog. It does not mark catalog entries installed, prove professional competence, or dispatch work to live company chats.

## Accountable owner and review
- Proposed accountable implementation role: `backend-dev` (Backend Dev).
- Architecture and compatibility reviewer: `chief-architect`.
- QA owns independent acceptance; domain reviewers evaluate specialist outputs; Release Engineer handles separately authorized distribution.
- These are logical repository roles, not GitHub usernames or new authority grants. No GitHub assignee is inferred.
- Governing definition revision for this planning assignment: `ae6080186ceb83cbdfd1b23bbfe532f8c0a678f4`. Candidate governance changes follow the existing adoption procedure.
- Evidence snapshot: 2026-10-19 (Asia/Tokyo).

## Current implementation status

Foundation design: [integration registry architecture](https://github.com/newbiesitl/paprika-inc/blob/49af108946ffc0c58792995302d1ea54ee40855b/docs/architecture/INTEGRATION-REGISTRY.md) and [packaged integration guide](https://github.com/newbiesitl/paprika-inc/blob/49af108946ffc0c58792995302d1ea54ee40855b/plugins/paprika-inc/skills/setup-paprika-inc/references/integrations.md).

## Dependencies and related work
- #29 — draft registry/pack foundation; prerequisite for adoption, not evidence that live adapters exist.
- #6 — optional pinned scientific research skills; reuse the existing research-core work.
- #14 — selective engineering and UX skill evaluation; reuse its source screening and acceptance work.
- #16 — Anthropic/Google/Meta agent-provider adapters. Those are model/agent runtime integrations; this issue concerns company presets, procedures, domain tools and workflows.
- #15 — standalone GUI; a future consumer of these contracts, not a prerequisite for the first native-tool slice.

## Integration model
1. **Company preset:** composition metadata, industry/business-model tags, role-template selections, workflow selections and required capabilities.
2. **Role template:** responsibilities, expected inputs/outputs, reviewer relationships and pack/workflow requirements. A role is a contract, not a tool entitlement.
3. **Skill pack:** versioned procedures and selected resources, with complete references, provenance and license obligations.
4. **Workflow template:** bounded steps, typed handoff artifacts, evidence and review points.
5. **Adapter:** typed operations over a native host capability, remote service or local worker.
6. **Private binding:** the actual authenticated account/tenant/connection; never part of a public persona.

B2B, B2C, SaaS, open source and nonprofit are composable business-model/organization overlays. For example, an applied-ML SaaS company can combine research, software, sales and operations roles.

A generic extension mechanism does not make every third-party package compatible. Unknown formats remain candidates until an adapter and acceptance evidence exist. Keep the portable manifest separate from the finite, implemented adapter types.

### Native delivery boundaries
- Use supported native GitHub tools or the official GitHub MCP server where available. A backend process cannot call a desktop's private tool namespace merely because a manifest names it: a host adapter must dispatch through an actual supported host capability, or use a separately configured service API.
- Package reusable procedures as supported native skills/plugins, with discovery and invocation evidence per host.
- Local Codex can use an explicitly supported local worker or MCP stdio boundary. ChatGPT access to local compute requires a reachable supported service such as remote MCP; it is not granted by copying a skill folder.
- Prefer existing compatible MCP servers over wrapping every service again. Add a wrapper when input/output normalization, constrained execution, provenance or missing domain operations justify it.
- Preserve current host permissions and repository governance. Keep credentials, real conversation contents, native chat IDs and private bindings out of public source.
- Keep vendor/paprika-messenger unchanged; domain computation must not be added to its communication-only service.

## Backend implementation backlog
All tasks are initially unchecked. P0–P4 are delivery phases for this tracker, not a GitHub milestone assignment. Backend Dev is the implementation owner unless a task narrows ownership; reviewers listed below are proposed review needs.

**G0 — baseline/schema review:** review and adopt the foundation in #29, including the extension contract. Code and CI evidence already exist in the draft PR, but merge/release remains separate. Design can proceed against the draft; dependent integration must use the reviewed baseline.

- [ ] G0: Record the reviewed foundation commit and schema decisions.

### BE-01 · P0 · Company preset and role-template contract
- [ ] Implementation and acceptance evidence recorded for BE-01.
- **Owner:** Backend Dev. **Review:** Chief Architect; Frontend Dev.
- **Depends on:** G0 schema review.
- **Scope:** Add versioned preset/role-template metadata: stable IDs, industry and business-model tags, responsibilities, inputs/outputs, reviewer roles, skill-pack IDs, workflow IDs and connector requirements. Compose through the existing author plan/write path; keep private bindings out of presets.
- **Acceptance:** Two fictional companies with different rosters compose without runtime code changes; missing references and conflicting selections fail clearly; existing user contracts and ownership files are preserved.

### BE-02 · P0 · Reviewed upstream selection and adaptation tooling
- [ ] Implementation and acceptance evidence recorded for BE-02.
- **Owner:** Backend Dev. **Review:** Chief Architect; QA.
- **Depends on:** G0 schema review.
- **Scope:** Build on the version-2 pack builder from #29. Record selected commit/file digests, license/notice obligations, transitive references, adaptation notes and host-specific exclusions. Convert reusable procedures/personas into Paprika-owned wrappers; do not import upstream governance, hooks or autonomous delegation automatically.
- **Acceptance:** One narrow upstream selection produces reproducible artifacts; source drift, missing references and duplicate discovery roots are rejected; a full provider-specific runtime cannot enter through the skill path.

### BE-03 · P1 · First marketing skill pack
- [ ] Implementation and acceptance evidence recorded for BE-03.
- **Owner:** Backend Dev. **Review:** Chief Architect; domain reviewer; QA.
- **Depends on:** BE-02.
- **Scope:** Adapt product-marketing context, copywriting and one SEO-analysis procedure into a bounded marketing-core candidate. Prefer user-supplied inputs for the first pilot; expose required context and optional integrations explicitly.
- **Acceptance:** An extracted package installs/reuses only selected files; fixed example briefs yield traceable outputs; cross-skill references resolve; missing external access is reported rather than invented.

### BE-04 · P1 · Native Codex and ChatGPT skill delivery
- [ ] Implementation and acceptance evidence recorded for BE-04.
- **Owner:** Backend Dev. **Review:** QA; Frontend Dev.
- **Depends on:** BE-03.
- **Scope:** Package the same selected workflow for each supported native surface. Verify native discovery and invocation using actual host-supported installation/configuration, preserving source/payload versions. Treat local project materialization and ChatGPT plugin delivery as separate capabilities.
- **Acceptance:** Record one real invocation on each claimed host, with exact host/package revision, inputs and output evidence. Unsupported accounts/surfaces remain unverified or blocked; local tests never mark ChatGPT ready.

### BE-05 · P0 · Typed integration invocation and result contract
- [ ] Implementation and acceptance evidence recorded for BE-05.
- **Owner:** Backend Dev. **Review:** Chief Architect; QA.
- **Depends on:** G0 schema review.
- **Scope:** Specify operation IDs, input/output schemas, capabilities, host requirements, read/write classification, operation correlation, timeouts, structured errors, artifact references and evidence. Keep the read-only registry separate from execution; prohibit arbitrary command strings as adapter implementations.
- **Acceptance:** Conformance fixtures cover valid/invalid inputs, unsupported hosts, missing capabilities, timeout/error/unknown outcomes and schema/version mismatch. A registry entry alone cannot invoke a tool or grant access.

### BE-06 · P0 · Private connections and authentication
- [ ] Implementation and acceptance evidence recorded for BE-06.
- **Owner:** Backend Dev. **Review:** Chief Architect; QA; Data Engineer when persistence is assigned.
- **Depends on:** BE-05.
- **Scope:** Bind integrations to observed native connections or supported credential storage. Define account/project/tenant scope, OAuth/token handling where applicable, expiry/revocation and permission checks. Reuse host-managed auth when available.
- **Acceptance:** Tests demonstrate missing/expired/revoked credentials, wrong-account/tenant isolation and redacted logs; secrets and actual bindings stay out of Git, role manifests, issue bodies and model-visible tool arguments.

### BE-07 · P1 · GitHub native connector adapter
- [ ] Implementation and acceptance evidence recorded for BE-07.
- **Owner:** Backend Dev. **Review:** Chief Architect; QA.
- **Depends on:** BE-05; BE-06.
- **Scope:** Reuse supported native GitHub tools or the official GitHub MCP server. Normalize repository identity, file/issue/PR retrieval and artifact references. Add explicit write operations only where authorized, with reconciliation before retrying an uncertain result.
- **Acceptance:** A real read-only task returns repository/commit-linked evidence. Tests cover pagination, missing permissions, stale refs and rate limits. A write fixture cannot duplicate an issue or PR after an unknown response.

### BE-08 · P2 · Local Python/CLI worker boundary
- [ ] Implementation and acceptance evidence recorded for BE-08.
- **Owner:** Backend Dev. **Review:** Chief Architect; QA.
- **Depends on:** BE-05.
- **Scope:** Implement allowlisted typed operations over pinned dependencies in isolated environments, with bounded inputs/outputs, timeout/cancellation and controlled file access. Use argument arrays and the selected operation schema; do not provide unrestricted shell execution. Local MCP stdio is an optional transport over this boundary.
- **Acceptance:** Fixtures cover invalid input, unavailable dependency, timeout, cancellation, excessive output and escaping paths. The same operation can be called independently of any industry persona.

### BE-09 · P2 · Remote MCP transport for domain tools
- [ ] Implementation and acceptance evidence recorded for BE-09.
- **Owner:** Backend Dev. **Review:** Chief Architect; QA.
- **Depends on:** BE-05; BE-06; BE-08 for compute tools.
- **Scope:** Expose selected typed operations through a supported MCP HTTP service for ChatGPT and Codex. Reuse existing compatible MCP services when sufficient. - **Acceptance:** Protocol/schema tests and a real host connection succeed for each claimed surface; auth and tool annotations reflect actual behavior; short work returns directly and long work returns a job reference.

- **Acceptance:** Known molecules match a pinned RDKit reference; invalid/oversized inputs and runtime failures are covered; the same fixture succeeds through local Codex and the remote MCP route.

### BE-15 · P3 · Finance, legal, HR and recruiting procedure packs
- [ ] Implementation and acceptance evidence recorded for BE-15.

- **Depends on:** BE-02; BE-04; BE-05/06 if tools are required.

Preserve source notices, assumptions, jurisdiction/data requirements and required review points; use user-supplied inputs before adding commercial-data/HRIS/ATS connectors.
- **Acceptance:** Track each of the four packs independently. Each has a complete resource closure, explicit unsupported features and a representative evaluated task. No source repository's marketing claim is accepted as performance evidence.

### BE-16 · P2 · Reusable workflow templates and resumable execution

- **Owner:** Backend Dev. **Review:** Chief Architect; QA; Data Engineer when state design is assigned.
- **Depends on:** BE-01; BE-05; BE-07 for repository workflows.

Reuse existing supported handoff/state mechanisms; distinguish drafts from effectful operations and reconcile unknown results before retry. Keep arbitrary DAG scheduling and autonomous background execution out of the first slice.

## Kickoff: shared company catalog, two UI surfaces, independent QA

**Owner direction (2026-10-19):** start the integration program; expose company structures, roles/personas and skills in the README and in a browse/select/configure interface on **both** native Codex/ChatGPT and standalone Paprika surfaces. Scoped kickoff briefs are authorized for the existing Backend, Frontend and QA chats.

The first delivery is a reviewable catalog/configuration slice. The remaining BE-02–BE-18 program stays visible above and proceeds in the established dependency order; this kickoff does not claim those integrations shipped.

### User journey
1. Open **Paprika Inc → Company catalog** in the native panel or standalone interface.
2. Search/filter company types; select a preset. Show supported/template-only/planned entries explicitly.
3. Choose an organization structure (for example, a lean team, functional departments or a research lab) and business-model tags independently of industry.
4. Add/remove role templates; inspect responsibilities, inputs/outputs, reporting relationships and independent reviewer relationships.
5. Select compatible skill packs and workflow templates per role. Show required tools, dependencies and host-specific limitations.
6. Configure company name/ID and repository/project through the host-supported selection route. Keep connection credentials out of the public catalog and exported configuration.
7. **Review configuration:** show the resulting roster, role/pack versions, ownership/review relationships, missing prerequisites and proposed file changes.
8. Save/export a portable draft; use existing protected author plan/write and supported bootstrap steps for separately requested application. Browsing or selection creates no live chats.

Use an accessible searchable picker for the primary preset, then a configuration panel for detail. Do not compress all role/skill/connector settings into one huge dropdown.

### Shared contract and status rules
- One versioned catalog drives CLI/MCP reads, README generation and both UI renderers. Do not maintain separate hard-coded option lists.
- Stable preset, structure, role, skill-pack and workflow IDs; versions; labels/descriptions; tags; referenced requirements; provenance; applicable host capabilities; evidence links.
- Distinguish role reporting relationships from reviewer relationships. Validate missing references, duplicates, cycles where forbidden and a review assignment to the same role.
- Separate **catalog availability**, **package presence**, **local configuration**, **connection/authentication**, **native host verification**, **task-quality acceptance** and **release state**. A successful source check cannot set all dimensions to ready.
- Minimum initial usable templates: existing IT/software and scientific-research blueprints, preserving selected research-core/engineering-core semantics. Additional industry entries can be browsed as planned; do not invent packaged skills for the 43-family roadmap.
- Proposed operations: list/search catalog; read exact entry; validate/preview selection; export portable blueprint. Backend may refine operation names during contract review. Mutations reuse existing authoring boundaries rather than adding an unrestricted remote filesystem operation.
- Keep a revision/digest in selection and preview results so stale selections are detected before application. Preserve edited company files and show conflicts.
- Native UI uses supported MCP Apps resources/bridge and capability detection. A plugin-owned dropdown is not a promise to modify the host's global menu. Plain tool/text and export routes remain available where UI rendering is unsupported.
- Reuse the same view model/components for the standalone interface and native panel; link the existing GUI work #15.
- No new public hosting, plugin installation, merge or release is included in this kickoff.

### CAT-BE-01 — Backend first slice (extends BE-01 and BE-05)
- [ ] **Owner: backend-dev. Review: chief-architect and frontend-dev; independent acceptance: QA.**
- Publish a small versioned schema/fixture proposal in this issue or a linked draft PR for QA/frontend review before fixing consequential interface decisions.
- Implement the generic preset/structure/role composition contract, catalog read/search and selection validation/preview/export over the existing authoring path.
- Provide typed, host-neutral results and explicit unsupported/missing prerequisites; preserve the read-only registry/execution separation.
- Supply backend fixtures for both baseline company types, missing dependencies, invalid reporting/reviewer graphs, stale revisions and existing-file conflicts.
- Use an isolated worktree/branch. The draft foundation #29 at `49af108946ffc0c58792995302d1ea54ee40855b` is a candidate dependency; stack explicitly or document a current-main equivalent. Do not edit its active worktree or merge it.
- Proportionate runtime tests, repository/plugin checks and diff check; open a draft PR with exact evidence and uncovered scope.
- Completion evidence: two different company configurations validate/export without an industry-specific runtime branch; existing files survive conflict cases; consumers share stable IDs and status semantics.

### CAT-FE-01 — Native and standalone catalog/configuration UI
- [ ] **Owner: frontend-dev. Review: chief-architect and backend-dev; independent acceptance: QA.**
- Build the browse/select/configure journey above on both requested surfaces from the shared catalog contract. Start the interaction model and fixture-driven view while the backend contract is reviewed.
- Implement keyboard-accessible search/picker controls, role/skill selection, structure display, configuration summary and dependency/status details.
- Cover loading, empty search, service failure, stale catalog, unavailable tool, unsupported host, conflicting selection and retained draft states. Do not mark planned integrations usable or silently remove user choices.
- Own README/homepage exposure generated or consistency-checked against the catalog. List what is supported today and link planned entries separately.
- Inspect the existing plugin/GUI sources and use supported MCP Apps/Extensions where justified; preserve plugin identity and hosting. No invented global host dropdown.
- Use a separate worktree and UI-owned files. Coordinate shared contract/schema changes through the draft PR/issue, not concurrent edits to backend files.
- Completion evidence: the same configuration is produced on native and standalone routes; keyboard/error/recovery checks and actual host evidence are recorded separately from browser fixtures. An unavailable host remains unverified.

### CAT-QA-01 — Acceptance design, then runnable-candidate validation
- [ ] **Owner: qa. Technical decision: chief-architect; implementation owners fix defects.**
- **Checkpoint A, now:** assess the proposed journey and contract for testability; publish a bounded acceptance matrix with concrete expected outcomes and blockers before consequential schema/UI choices are fixed.
- **Checkpoint B, runnable candidate:** test exact Backend/Frontend commits and extracted package artifacts. Record actual Codex, ChatGPT and standalone results separately. A normal browser screenshot cannot certify native rendering.
- Cover: both baseline presets; optional/required roles; role/pack dependencies; independent reviewer handling; structure graph validation; missing auth/tool/host capability; planned-item status; invalid/stale selection; conflict-safe authoring; keyboard/focus/labels; empty/error/retry behavior; draft recovery; README/catalog consistency; supported fallback when the native panel is unavailable.
- Evaluate **functional correctness** separately from **task quality**. Later connector pilots require expected-answer fixtures (for example, repository/commit identity for GitHub and verified constraint satisfaction and solver status for OR-Tools), plus failure/retry/auth isolation evidence. Persona prose alone does not pass a domain task.
- Report passed/failed/not tested/blocked checks with exact inputs, candidate revision, environment and reproduction steps; classify merge-blocking defects separately from suggestions.
- Batch tests per meaningful checkpoint; after fixes, retest affected behavior and relevant regressions. Do not rerun unchanged suites solely because another commit exists.
- QA must not independently approve implementation it authored. No merge/release acceptance until required evidence is met; unavailable environments remain explicit.

### Coordination for this slice
The Chief Architect owns the common contract decision and collects the three scoped reports from their existing chats and this issue. Backend owns canonical catalog/schema/runtime files; Frontend owns UI/README exposure; QA owns the independent acceptance matrix/evidence. Keep existing human-assigned role names and governance unchanged. This is a technical kickoff, not a new standing coordinator role.

Keep public progress and cross-role interface discussion in this tracker/linked PRs. Native kickoff delivery, implementation progress, independent acceptance and release are separate states. The sending chat will read role results; the brief itself grants no new peer-message permission or background automation.

**Kickoff status (2026-10-19):** scoped briefs were submitted through the existing Paprika Inc native delivery workflow to Backend Dev, Frontend Dev and QA. Native status observations confirm all three began their assigned work. QA is preparing checkpoint A, Backend is preparing schema/fixtures, and Frontend is inspecting the shared UI approach. Implementation, independent acceptance and release remain open; this is delivery/start evidence only.

Native UI references: [MCP Apps UI](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/chatgpt-ui), [MCP server/UI quickstart](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/app-quickstart), [host Extensions](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/extensions).

## Completion and evidence requirements
- [ ] Reviewed versioned contracts compose at least two different company presets without runtime branches per industry.
- [ ] Existing research-core/engineering-core behavior and existing authored company files are preserved.
- [ ] A native skill, a service connector and a compute wrapper each pass their own acceptance criteria.
- [ ] Every claimed Codex/ChatGPT combination has actual discovery, authentication (where needed), invocation and output evidence; untested combinations remain explicit.
- [ ] Each adopted source has a pinned revision, selected inventory, license/notice record, complete resource closure and adaptation notes.
- [ ] Native-tool reuse, remote MCP and local execution are distinguishable in compatibility reports.
- [ ] Missing permissions, wrong tenant, invalid input, timeout, cancellation and uncertain write/job outcomes are covered by relevant tests.
- [ ] Workflow resume preserves evidence and review state without duplicate effects.
- [ ] QA records task-quality results against representative fixed baselines, including misses, false positives and collateral actions.
- [ ] For source/definition changes, run the repository validator and git diff --check; add meaningful behavior tests for runtime changes and required plugin/package checks. Documentation checks are not runtime certification.
- [ ] Update/rollback tests preserve user edits and private bindings; release evidence names the distributed version.
- [ ] Selected presets resolve accepted dependencies. The broad catalog may retain deferred entries with explicit follow-up work; it must not imply every proposed industry is shipped.

**Evidence record per slice:** source revision/inventory → adaptation PR → local/CI results → native host/package version → connection scope without secrets → fixed task inputs → output/artifact references → QA/domain review → release/version or explicit unverified status.

This tracker may be split into child issues when implementation slices are assigned. Keep the checklist and evidence links here as the program index; creating the tracker itself does not assign or message live agents.

## CAT-QA-01 — Checkpoint A: acceptance matrix and contract decisions

**QA result: acceptance design prepared; contract sign-off remains pending the decisions below.** This is a design review, not a runtime pass or approval of draft #29.

- Governing definition: `ae6080186ceb83cbdfd1b23bbfe532f8c0a678f4`.
- Foundation inspected: #29 at `49af108946ffc0c58792995302d1ea54ee40855b`; treated as a draft dependency, not adopted authority.
- Scope: shared catalog/configuration contract, README, native Codex, native ChatGPT, and standalone UI. Each native host receives a separate result.
- Owner: QA. Technical decisions/return collection: Chief Architect; Backend and Frontend implement fixes. No production changes, installations, live chat creation, or suite execution in this checkpoint.

### Decisions needed before the contract is fixed

**D1 — Define graph types and composition rules (Backend + Chief Architect).** Reporting edges, ownership, and reviewer relationships need separate validation. The existing IT blueprint has reciprocal architect/QA reviewers; the research blueprint has reciprocal researcher/scientific-reviewer relationships. A blanket “reject all cycles” rule would reject both baseline templates. Reject reporting cycles where the chosen structure forbids them and reject self-review/dangling reviewers; permit valid reciprocal peer review. Define required versus optional roles, reporting cardinality, and what happens to dependent references when a role is removed. Empty reviewer lists must expose the permitted human-review fallback rather than imply independent agent acceptance. Sources: [IT baseline](https://github.com/newbiesitl/paprika-inc/blob/49af108946ffc0c58792995302d1ea54ee40855b/plugins/paprika-inc/skills/setup-paprika-inc/assets/it-company-blueprint.json), [research baseline](https://github.com/newbiesitl/paprika-inc/blob/49af108946ffc0c58792995302d1ea54ee40855b/plugins/paprika-inc/skills/setup-paprika-inc/assets/research-company-blueprint.json).

**D2 — Define the lossless draft-to-blueprint boundary (Backend + Frontend).** The foundation's [authoring schema](https://github.com/newbiesitl/paprika-inc/blob/49af108946ffc0c58792995302d1ea54ee40855b/plugins/paprika-inc/runtime/paprika-inc/authoring.mjs) accepts a fixed company/role field set; it does not accept structure, reporting edges, business-model tags, workflow selections, or selection-revision fields. Choose a versioned draft/envelope and an explicit translation or compatible schema extension. Preserve these choices across export/reopen; do not silently drop them or pass unsupported fields to authoring. Distinguish a saved incomplete draft from an authorable blueprint. A missing local installation need not invalidate a portable draft, while an unknown/unbundled pack cannot become a valid installed-pack claim.

**D3 — Define evidence/status ownership and invalidation (Backend + Frontend + Chief Architect).** Publish the status vocabulary, reason codes, evidence identity, and refresh rules for each dimension. In #29, `declared-compatible` expressly retains `installed: false`, `authentication_verified: false`, and `runtime_verified: false`; mapping it to “ready” would be incorrect. Define when a changed catalog, package, selected host, connection, or configuration invalidates an observation. Carry catalog/selection revision through preview and recheck it at any later application boundary.

These are testability dependencies, not findings that an unimplemented UI has failed. Fixture-driven UI work can proceed while the contract examples are reviewed.

### Acceptance matrix

Every executable row below is **NOT TESTED** at checkpoint A: no catalog/UI candidate has been supplied. Rows marked D1–D3 also depend on the corresponding contract decision. “Both UI routes” means identical functional expectations on standalone and each claimed native host; browser fixtures alone do not satisfy native evidence.

| ID | Concrete input/action | Required outcome | Checkpoint B evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CAT-01 | Load the pinned IT and scientific-research presets without edits. | IT exports its five roles; research exports its four roles. Stable role IDs, reviewer/ownership references and selected research-core/engineering-core semantics survive. The same generic composition path handles both. | Backend fixtures, normalized exports, extracted-package check. |
| CAT-02 | Select IT with lean/functional structures and research with a lab structure; change business-model tags independently. | Industry, structure and tags remain separate choices. Each supported combination has explicit reporting edges; unsupported combinations explain the incompatibility. Changing structure does not silently erase role edits. D1/D2. | Contract examples and UI round-trips. |
| CAT-03 | Rename a role label; remove a coordinator/required role; remove an optional unreferenced role; duplicate an instance ID. | Labels do not change identity. Required-role removal and duplicate IDs produce field-specific errors. Optional removal works when valid. Dependent ownership/reviewer/skill links require visible repair, never silent deletion. D1. | Negative fixtures and editable UI errors. |
| CAT-04 | Supply a reporting cycle, missing manager, dangling reviewer, self-review, reciprocal peer reviewers and overlapping ownership paths. | Enforce each graph's declared rules; reject invalid references/self-review/ownership collisions; retain valid reciprocal reviewers. Rendering reporting lines never reassigns reviewers. Role metadata alone does not establish actual review independence. D1. | Typed error paths plus structure/summary UI. |
| CAT-05 | Add/remove research-core and engineering-core; select a workflow requiring a missing pack/tool; select an unknown pack/version. | Dependencies are explained per role/workflow. Required versus optional prerequisites remain distinguishable. Preserve the choice as an incomplete draft where allowed; do not claim an invalid selection is authorable, installed or executable. No automatic install/authentication. D2/D3. | Dependency fixtures and both UI routes. |
| CAT-06 | Open a planned industry, candidate integration, packaged-but-not-installed skill, and declared-compatible integration. | Planned/template/packaged states remain distinct from installed, authenticated, host-verified, task-accepted and released. No blanket green “ready”; unknown evidence is visible. Browsing a roadmap item remains possible without inventing a usable pack. D3. | One mixed-state fixture and screenshots/text output per surface. |
| CAT-07 | Keep the same selection while changing Codex/ChatGPT/standalone context; simulate missing tools, absent/revoked auth and stale evidence. | Results are scoped to the selected host/connection. Report the exact missing prerequisite and preserve the draft. A local worker declaration does not prove ChatGPT access; a connected tool does not prove task-quality acceptance. D3. | Capability/error fixtures; actual discovery/invocation evidence only for claimed routes. |
| CAT-08 | Search/filter by label, tag and stable ID; use Unicode, no matches, clear filters and multiple response pages where supported. | Deterministic complete results without duplicate/lost IDs; clear empty state; selection survives filtering. Delayed old responses cannot replace results for the current query. | Shared read/search tests and UI interaction trace. |
| CAT-09 | Preview at revision R1; change catalog, pack/version or selection to R2 before export/application. | Detect stale input with actionable reasons. Preserve user edits; refresh/diff explicitly. No old preview can authorize new content. Define canonical ordering/digest and round-trip equality. D2/D3. | Revision-mismatch fixtures and both UI routes. |
| CAT-10 | Preview against edited company files; change/create a target after preview; fail a later write in a disposable fixture. | Existing protected authoring is reused. Browsing/preview/export do not apply files. Separately requested application rechecks conflicts and preserves edited files. Partial creation reports exact created/conflicting paths for reconciliation; retry cannot silently overwrite them. | Isolated filesystem tests and preview diff. No production application needed. |
| CAT-11 | Save/export and reopen the same customized configuration on each surface; encounter an unsupported schema/version. | Preserve stable IDs, versions, structure, review/ownership relationships and selections. Equal input/catalog revisions yield equivalent normalized output. Unsupported versions fail visibly without data loss. Export excludes credentials, native chat IDs and machine paths. D2. | Export/import fixtures, cross-surface comparison and extracted package. |
| CAT-12 | Navigate picker/configuration/review using only keyboard: Tab/Shift-Tab, arrows, Enter/Space, Escape. | Visible focus, named controls, announced selection/error/loading states, no keyboard trap or unintended activation. Closing a picker returns focus to its trigger; validation reaches the invalid field while retaining entries. Disabled choices have an accessible reason. | Keyboard interaction evidence on standalone and each rendered native host; accessibility-tree checks where available. |
| CAT-13 | Exercise loading, empty catalog, service error, timeout, retry, cancellation, late response and refresh/navigation during edits. | Distinct states and useful retry path; draft edits retained. Old responses cannot overwrite newer selections. Read retries create no effects. An uncertain write is reconciled rather than repeated. Define actual persistence scope; closing a native view must not imply durable storage without evidence. D2. | Controlled failures plus draft recovery trace. |
| CAT-14 | Native UI resource/bridge absent, unsupported or failing. | Advertise the limitation; provide supported tool/text/export fallback from the same contract. Do not invent a global host dropdown, silently launch another host, or treat fallback success as native panel success. | Host-capability fixtures and actual unavailable-host observation. |
| CAT-15 | Compare README/homepage, catalog read results, native UI and standalone at the same revision; change a catalog status/label/version. | One canonical inventory or deterministic consistency check catches drift. Supported items are separated from the 43-family roadmap; catalog counts are data, not parallel hard-coded lists. Private connection/host state does not leak into public README. | Generation/parity check with a deliberate mismatch. |
| CAT-16 | Feed malformed IDs, unknown references, oversized fields and labels containing markup/control text; inspect export and side effects. | Bounded field-specific rejection or safe display; labels cannot execute code/change routing. No implicit native chats, messages, subscriptions, connector execution, hosting or installation. Public artifacts remain free of private bindings. | Input validation, rendered text and controlled effect inspection. |
| CAT-17 | Run the exact packaged candidate extracted outside the source checkout; load both baseline configurations. | Required catalog/schema/UI assets and references are present. Results agree with source; no accidental dependence on repository/vendor paths. Package identity/digest is recorded. | Extracted-package checks plus separately recorded real-host evidence. |

### Evidence and gate rules

For each result record: matrix ID, fixture/input revision, Backend and Frontend commit SHAs, catalog schema/revision/digest, extracted package SHA256, host/app/browser version, steps, expected versus actual, and **PASS / FAIL / NOT TESTED / BLOCKED** with a reason. Keep real identities, credentials, conversation content and raw private evidence out of this public issue; publish sanitized findings.

Track these dimensions separately:

| Dimension | Evidence needed; prohibited inference |
| --- | --- |
| Catalog availability | Exact preset/role/pack/workflow metadata and declared maturity; listed does not mean packaged. |
| Package presence | Exact bundled and/or installed payload/version, distinguishing the two; source metadata does not prove either. |
| Local configuration | Observation of the intended project's actual selected settings; packaged or installed does not mean configured. |
| Connection/authentication | Observation for the intended private connection/host; metadata or a fixture cannot establish access. |
| Native host verification | Actual resource/tool discovery and use on each named host/version; a browser screenshot proves only that browser route. |
| Task-quality acceptance | Fixed representative task, expected output and independent/domain review; successful UI selection or persona prose is insufficient. |
| Release state | Explicit distributed version and release evidence; passing tests or an open PR cannot mark a release. |

**Checkpoint A status:** PASS — scope/source review and bounded matrix prepared. BLOCKED — contract sign-off for D1–D3 until example inputs/results resolve them. NOT TESTED — all runnable catalog/UI/package cases and actual host combinations. FAIL — none established by this design-only review.

## CAT-QA-01 / INT-QA-01 — decision review and integration acceptance extension

This supplements the [checkpoint A matrix](https://github.com/newbiesitl/paprika-inc/issues/30#issuecomment-6260944113). Existing CAT-01–CAT-17 gates remain. **RDKit is optional/future under #32; OR-Tools replaces it as the current compute pilot.** GitHub, MLflow and ERPNext/Frappe are the current service integrations.

Governing definition remains `ae6080186ceb83cbdfd1b23bbfe532f8c0a678f4`. Reviewed the [architecture decisions](https://github.com/newbiesitl/paprika-inc/issues/30#issuecomment-6261066602), #31's committed proposal at `f99c64ae9f071eeae0682f3475b93c5281ad19ce`, and the in-progress contract/document edits read-only. Working edits are not immutable acceptance evidence.

### Catalog decision review

| Decision | Design assessment | Evidence still needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D1: separate graphs | **PASS at design level.** Draft documentation specifies a coordinator-rooted reporting tree, flat direct edges, allowed reciprocal peer reviewers, and invalid self/dangling/duplicate edges. Catalog declares required roles. | Show valid reciprocal review, invalid reporting cycle, required-role removal, optional removal with retained unresolved references, and explicit human-review fallback. Preserve baseline ownership reviewers independently of role-review edges. |
| D2: portable envelope and labels | **PASS at decision level; committed examples pending.** Selection plus schema-1 blueprint preserves configuration-only choices. The pinned wire contract has no title override; current working edits add `title?: string` and roster review requirements. | Commit title mapping and fixtures: absent/default title, customized title round-trip, blank/multiline/over-limit rejection, and stable role ID. Define the 160-character counting rule and test Unicode boundaries. Save/reopen an invalid draft without silently repairing it; authorable export still requires validation. |
| D3: evidence boundaries | **PASS at design level for configuration operations.** Wire results keep auth/native/task states unverified and release draft; requirements are unknown/missing/declared-present/unsupported. This matches the decision. | Response examples for absent versus empty capability observations, host switch, catalog mismatch and changed selection; stale results must not replace current UI state. Any later runtime-verified label requires the separate identity/provenance/invalidation contract before use. |

Static fixture check: both baseline selections contain the expected 5/4 roles and match catalog digest `2ae9bf4c5dafb58948e38c1d8be8d7bc9dad1d2ad7465dcec585f45068f814d5`; the stale-selection fixture deliberately differs. The six committed fixtures contain no title-override or empty-reviewer example and no expected-result snapshots for those cases. These are pending evidence, not an executed runtime failure.

Thus the architectural ambiguity in D1–D3 is resolved; **independent implementation acceptance stays open** until the committed contract/examples and behavior are verified.

### Bounded integration matrix

All integration execution rows below are currently **NOT TESTED**. They define expected outcomes, not claims that services or credentials are available.

| ID | Concrete case | Acceptance / evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| INT-01 | Invoke one declared read/compute operation with valid, malformed and oversized input; request an unknown operation or unsupported host. | Versioned typed result/error, stable operation correlation and explicit completeness; invalid calls cause no service/worker execution. Record adapter/package version, input identity and observed execution route. A named adapter alone is not executable evidence. |
| GH-01 | Read an existing accessible repository at immutable commit C and another known revision; inspect issue/PR identity. Simulate a moving branch in the protocol fixture. | Repository identity and C remain explicit. File/blob evidence belongs to C; issue/PR snapshots retain their own IDs, observation time and PR head where relevant. Do not claim mutable issue data is a commit snapshot. Compare against authoritative read results. |
| GH-02 | Use more records than one page; inject repeated/invalid next links, page-two failure, rate limit and wrong repository scope. | Follow the selected route's real pagination contract; detect loops, preserve filters/scope, and bound pages/time. Either finish or report partial/truncated/error with resumable context—never silently label the first page complete. Cross-origin next links must not receive credentials. GitHub REST uses returned link relations; connector routes must use their own observed contract. [GitHub pagination](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api). |
| ML-01 | Seed an actual local MLflow instance with two experiments, distinct run IDs sharing a display name, known metric points and a small artifact. | Retrieve the correct experiment/run, compare metric key/value/step/time and artifact identity. Latest-value summaries must not masquerade as complete history. Paginate the operations supported by the pinned server version; verify artifact bytes/digest when retrieval is implemented, without executing them. [MLflow REST](https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/api_reference/rest-api.html). |
| ML-02 | Query a missing/deleted run; fail a later page; change private connection; deny access to a second experiment/service. | Missing resources, partial results, transport errors and authorization failures remain distinguishable. No cache or result crosses connection identity. An unauthenticated localhost instance can prove data-path behavior only; auth/isolation requires an enforcing test configuration or remains BLOCKED. |
| OR-01 | Actual solver: one machine, non-preemptive jobs A=2 and B=3, A before B, earliest start 0, hard finish horizon 5, minimize makespan. | Independent oracle: feasible optimum 5; A=[0,2), B=[2,5). Validate every job, duration, precedence and resource constraint in returned output, rather than merely trusting a success flag. Record OR-Tools version, solver type, model/input digest, parameters, objective and bounds where supported. |
| OR-02 | Same scheduling model with hard finish horizon 4; separately supply invalid job references, negative durations and unsupported numeric ranges. | The contradictory valid model is infeasible; malformed input/model is a validation failure, not “infeasible.” For CP-SAT preserve native OPTIMAL, FEASIBLE, INFEASIBLE, MODEL_INVALID and UNKNOWN semantics. Another solver choice needs an explicit equivalent mapping. [Solver status definitions](https://developers.google.com/optimization/cp/cp_solver). |
| OR-03 | Run a bounded harder instance; exercise deadline and cancellation, including stopping with and without a feasible incumbent. | Keep solver status separate from termination reason. A valid incumbent without proof may be feasible, not optimal; no incumbent before a limit is not proof of infeasibility. Validate any retained incumbent independently. Record actual stop evidence and wall time; cancellation stops work or truthfully reports stop pending. Do not claim a real time-limit branch was tested if the solver finished early. [CP-SAT limits/status](https://developers.google.com/optimization/cp/cp_solver). |
| ERP-01 | Seed a disposable ERPNext/Frappe instance with known inventory/work-order records across companies; read them by ID and through multiple pages. | Compare selected fields, units/status, document identity and modification/version evidence against seeded records. Listing uses stable ordering and the pinned API's pagination; no silent gaps/duplicates/completeness claims. A Frappe-only generic DocType demo does not certify ERPNext inventory/work-order semantics. [Frappe REST](https://docs.frappe.io/framework/user/en/api/rest). |
| ERP-02 | Two restricted principals and separate company/site scopes; attempt permitted and forbidden list/detail reads; revoke a credential. | Only authorized records/fields are returned; company filtering is not a substitute for service permissions. Direct ID lookup must not bypass list restrictions. Cache/cursors cannot carry scope across principals/sites. Confirm actual service enforcement; stubs cannot establish tenant isolation. [Frappe authenticated-user roles](https://docs.frappe.io/framework/user/en/api/rest). |
| INT-02 | Missing, wrong and revoked auth; switch endpoints/accounts; inspect diagnostics and exported configuration. | No silent use of another account, privileged fallback, or credentials in URLs/logs/export. Permission failure is not successful empty data. Bind observations/results to the intended private connection, represented publicly only by non-secret test aliases. |
| INT-03 | Timeout before response and after partial pagination, transient 5xx/rate limit, malformed payload, cancel then retry/reopen. | Published deadline/retry/response-size limits are enforced; retries preserve operation/scope and obey server delay where supplied. Report partial versus completed results. A read-only semantic operation may use POST; test allowed operations/effects rather than assuming every POST is a mutation. Worker/job uncertainty requires reconciliation without duplicate work. |
| INT-04 | Open the same integration/configuration via standalone, native Codex and native ChatGPT; request a route without its tool/worker/bridge. | Actual executable operation is wired to the catalog requirement and common result model. Unsupported routes retain explicit fallback/unverified state. Local CLI or browser success cannot set native-host verification; no new host route is inferred from a registry string. |
| INT-05 | Refresh catalog/UI/README after local successes; inspect the four current integrations and optional RDKit. | GitHub/MLflow/OR-Tools/ERPNext states reflect the evidence actually obtained. RDKit stays optional/planned, unselected and non-blocking. Distinguish implemented, local-service-tested, native-host-verified and released; source checks or stubs cannot promote later states. |
| INT-06 | Extract exact Backend/UI package candidates outside source checkout; repeat one representative service read and schedule. | Required schemas/adapters/assets/worker dependencies are present or explicitly declared; package behavior agrees with source. Pin candidate SHAs and package digest. No dependence on the developer's checkout or accidental production binding. |

The tiny scheduling inputs and expected answers above are QA test proposals. If the chosen operation schema cannot express these constraints, publish an equivalent independently checkable example before testing.

### Evidence boundaries and next checkpoint

Use explicit evidence labels alongside PASS/FAIL/NOT TESTED/BLOCKED:

- **Stub/protocol:** scripted response or browser bridge harness. Useful for failure branches; proves neither actual service behavior nor a native host.
- **Actual disposable service/library:** pinned MLflow server, ERPNext+Frappe stack, or real OR-Tools execution with seeded inputs. Record versions, setup, output and cleanup. This proves that local route only.
- **Actual GitHub read:** selected real GitHub connector/API route with repository/ref provenance; a local Git repository or mock HTTP server is not live GitHub evidence.
- **Actual native/standalone route:** each target independently shows discovery, permitted invocation, output and error handling. No production claim or release inference.

Before checkpoint B, supply exact PR heads/artifact hashes; operation schemas and status mapping; limits/retry/cancel policy; disposable-service startup/teardown; seeded expected results; the supported authentication model; and which hosts are available. Attempt a real disposable ERPNext/Frappe environment with supported tooling when the runnable adapter is ready. If unavailable, record the exact blocker, continue protocol checks, and leave full-service/auth/tenant acceptance open.

Environment dependency: the [Architect's latest observation](https://github.com/newbiesitl/paprika-inc/issues/30#issuecomment-6261123540) reports no Docker/Podman command on PATH and no installed WSL. QA has not independently rerun that environment check. Recheck any explicitly configured alternative at checkpoint B; do not substitute a stub for full ERPNext/Frappe acceptance or infer permission to install an OS/runtime.

Public reports retain sanitized fixture IDs and results; real credentials, endpoint bindings and raw private logs stay private. No production fixtures, remote publishing, peer messages or deployment are part of this QA assignment.

**Current result:** PASS — design decisions reviewed and matrix extended; static catalog/fixture identity checks passed. NOT TESTED — executable connector, solver, UI/package and host acceptance. BLOCKED — full acceptance pending immutable updated examples and runnable candidates/service access. FAIL — no runtime defect established in this design-only checkpoint. This comment does not approve #29/#31 or close CAT/INT acceptance.
